Detailed Description

The QRM&CI pipeline stages as free functions: choosing a backend, compiling a task for it, submitting it to a device, collecting its result, and reporting a cancellation.

An entrypoint composes these into whatever loop it needs; none of them owns state of its own.

◆ buildQuantumResult()

std::expected< mqss::QuantumResult, Error > mqss::qrmci::buildQuantumResult ( const mqss::QuantumTask & task,
const std::vector< std::optional< mqss::submitter::Counts > > & histogram )
nodiscard

Build a QuantumResult from a task and its job-result histogram, the shared tail end of submitQuantumTask()+collectQuantumResult() and executeQuantumTask().

histogram's length must equal task's circuit file count, and every entry must carry counts: cardinality is preserved rather than collapsed, so the result has exactly one entry per circuit, in the same order, on success. Every count must also fit in the wire format's int32_t. Validated up front, before anything is written to the result, so a failure never returns a partially assembled QuantumResult.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task the histogram belongs to (used to populate the result's task/destination/QPU fields).
histogramOne counts map per circuit file, or nullopt for a circuit that produced no counts.
Returns
An expected QuantumResult containing one result entry per circuit, or a DeviceError if the histogram's length does not match the task's circuit count, any entry is nullopt, or any count exceeds INT32_MAX – each case naming the offending circuit index, or bitstring and value.

◆ chooseBackend()

std::expected< std::string, Error > mqss::qrmci::chooseBackend ( const mqss::QuantumTask & task,
const BackendRegistry & availableBackends,
BackendSelectionPolicy policy = BackendSelectionPolicy::LowestName )
nodiscard

Choose the backend that should execute a quantum task.

A pure query: it neither reads nor writes the task's scheduled QPU, so the caller assigns the returned name itself. The task's preferred QPU wins whenever it is registered, online and able to run the task; otherwise policy picks among every backend that can, deterministically.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task to choose a backend for.
availableBackendsThe backends to choose from.
policyThe rule for picking among several compatible backends.
Returns
The name of the chosen backend, or a NoBackendAvailable error if no suitable backend is found.

Collect the results of previously submitted quantum jobs.

Pairs with submitQuantumTask(); see that function's documentation for why the two are split apart.

Uninterruptible: unsuitable for a daemon work loop that must shut down promptly. Delegates to the four-argument overload with a flag that is never set.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task the jobs were submitted for (used to populate the result's task/destination/QPU fields).
jobsThe jobs returned by submitQuantumTask(), waited on in order.
waitTimeoutHow long to wait for each job; zero waits indefinitely.
Returns
An expected QuantumResult containing one result entry per job, or a DeviceError if a wait or a counts read failed, if a job finished in any state other than Done, or if a count exceeds INT32_MAX (buildQuantumResult()'s own checks; jobs' length already matches the task's circuit count here, so cardinality itself cannot mismatch).

◆ collectQuantumResult() [2/2]

std::expected< mqss::QuantumResult, Error > mqss::qrmci::collectQuantumResult ( const mqss::QuantumTask & task,
std::vector< mqss::submitter::Job > & jobs,
std::chrono::seconds waitTimeout,
const std::atomic< bool > & terminationFlag )
nodiscard

Interruptible overload of collectQuantumResult(), for a daemon work loop composing its own termination flag.

Each job is waited on in slices of at most one second rather than in one blocking call, so terminationFlag is checked, and a shutdown honoured, between slices instead of only before the whole wait. A zero waitTimeout still waits indefinitely absent a shutdown, but is now interruptible rather than truly unbounded; a positive waitTimeout still times out at the same total deadline as the three-argument overload.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task the jobs were submitted for.
jobsThe jobs returned by submitQuantumTask(), waited on in order.
waitTimeoutHow long to wait for each job; zero waits indefinitely.
terminationFlagConsulted before every wait slice.
Returns
An expected QuantumResult as the three-argument overload describes, or ShutdownRequested if terminationFlag was set before every job finished.

◆ submitQuantumTask() [1/2]

std::expected< std::vector< mqss::submitter::Job >, Error > mqss::qrmci::submitQuantumTask ( const mqss::QuantumTask & task,
const mqss::submitter::Device & device )
nodiscard

Submit the quantum task's circuits to the device without waiting for their results.

Pairs with collectQuantumResult() to let a caller submit several tasks back-to-back before collecting any of their results (pipelined batch submission), instead of blocking on each task's result in turn the way executeQuantumTask() does.

A Job carries exactly one payload, so a task with N circuit files becomes N jobs, submitted in the files' own order and returned in that order. The first submission failure short-circuits without waiting on or collecting any job already submitted for this task.

Uninterruptible: unsuitable for a daemon work loop that must shut down promptly. Delegates to the three-argument overload with a flag that is never set.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task to submit.
deviceThe device to submit to.
Returns
The submitted jobs, one per circuit file, or a SubmissionFailed error – which also covers a task with no circuit files or a zero shot count, both refused before the device is touched.

◆ submitQuantumTask() [2/2]

std::expected< std::vector< mqss::submitter::Job >, Error > mqss::qrmci::submitQuantumTask ( const mqss::QuantumTask & task,
const mqss::submitter::Device & device,
const std::atomic< bool > & terminationFlag )
nodiscard

Interruptible overload of submitQuantumTask(), for a daemon work loop composing its own termination flag.

terminationFlag is checked before each circuit's submission. If it is set, every job already submitted for this task is best-effort cancelled (a cancellation failure is logged, not propagated) and the call returns Error::Kind::ShutdownRequested instead of submitting the rest.

Parameters
taskThe quantum task to submit.
deviceThe device to submit to.
terminationFlagConsulted before every circuit submission.
Returns
The submitted jobs, one per circuit file; a SubmissionFailed error as the two-argument overload describes; or ShutdownRequested if terminationFlag was set before every circuit could be submitted.
